key_insight: LLMs can generate correct finite element code, but reliable scientific automation requires consistency across attempts and independent verification.
engineering_relevance: Automating nonlinear mechanics and structural dynamics coding is promising, but passing self-generated checks does not establish numerical correctness.
method: Extend FEM-Bench to 17 nonlinear, history-dependent mechanics and structural dynamics tasks.
Evaluate 15 models on implementation and test generation without execution feedback.
Compare two execution-enabled agentic harnesses for six models and analyze 249 failed trajectories.
evidence_signal: An exploratory separate coder–tester configuration achieved the highest observed scores: 97.6% probability of at least one success in three attempts and 88.8% probability that all three succeed.
watch_item: Agentic gains varied and regressions occurred; in 28.5% of failed trajectories, tests shared an error with the implementation.
paper_title: Scientific Coding with Large Language Models: Evidence from Finite Element Analysis
